question: The marks of furrows were discovered at the Harappan site in ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalibangan**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The marks of furrows were discovered in the** Kalibangan site of Indus valley currently Rajasthan.**
 
• This shows that the fields were **ploughed during Harappan Civilization.**
 
• A **wooden furrow **was found on that site.
 
• **Harappan seals, unknown scripts, stamps, human skeletons, copper bangles, coins, beads, toys, terracotta and shells **were also found at the Harappa site while excavation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lothal** is one of the southernmost sites of the ancient Indus valley civilization.
 
• It was a small **Harappan site found in Gujrat near the Gulf Of Khambat.**
 
• It was first excavated in **1957 by S R Rao.**
 
• **Dholavira-** The site of the Indus valley civilisation is considered to be the **second largest Harappan site in India and the fifth largest in the Indian subcontinent.**
 
• **Bhansali- **It was the** Harappan site currently located in Fatehabad district Haryana.** Beads** **of semi-precious stones, **terracotta, steatite and bangles of clay, shell, faience and copper **are some of the findings on this site.
